text:
Maya: Quick follow-up to the quant profiles RFC — hit a case where loader-side post-load requant flips dtypes after runtime selected kernels, causing assertion failures during serve. Need a short design patch.
Sanjay: seen this in a noisy canary. It's primarily an ordering/contract mismatch between loader and kernel allocator.
Jordan: agree. We should formalize a tiny handshake: loader declares intent, runtime replies with support vector, loader either adjusts or asks for rebind. Make it cheap (one-shot at load).
Priya: can we avoid a full rebind for small per-layer tweaks? rebind can be heavy on warmup.
Jordan: we can allow two modes: "declarative-reserve" (runtime reserves kernels for a set of bitwidths) and "force-rebind" (loader asks runtime to re-evaluate kernels). The manifest chooses.
Maya: concrete manifest example I drafted for ops/security review: 
```json
{"quant_negotiation": "1.0", "allowed_bitwidths": ["fp8","int8","4bit"], "mode": "declarative-reserve", "max_rebind_ms": 300, "fallback_chain": ["int8_safety","fp16_fallback"]}
```
Sanjay: +1. A few edge questions: who takes the latency hit if rebind happens? what if runtime refuses due to SLO?
Jordan: loader includes max_rebind_ms; runtime can accept or reply with REFUSE_REBIND. If refused loader can either drop to a compatible on-disk profile or offload to hosted fallback. We return structured codes for automation.
Maya: propose error payload for ops automation: 
```json
{"code":"QUANT_HANDSHAKE_FAIL","reason":"kernel-set-unavailable","allowed":"int8_safety,fp16_fallback","action":"auto-fallback"}
```
Priya: For observability, we should emit quant_handshake_latency, kernels_reserved_count, actual_bind_ms, and a boolean fallback_triggered. Ops needs tags: model_id, quant_profile, device_type.
Sanjay: Agree. Also add a quick compat-check API that does not allocate kernels, just returns true/false for a manifest header — used in CI/preflight. e.g. runtime.can_support(manifest_header) -> bool.
Jordan: For testing: QA will need a harness that simulates loader transformations (noop->requant->fallback) and asserts kernel cache correctness. We should add unit tests and an integration canary with warmup traffic.
Maya: Can we add a safety hysteresis so rapid repeated load/rebind cycles don't thrash kernels? maybe a simple token-bucket per model with cooldown_ms.
Priya: yes, include "hysteresis_ms" in manifest; runtime enforces.
Sanjay: Ops playbook item: if quant_handshake_latency > 500ms during warmup, mute canary and rollback. Add alert on handshake_fail_rate > 1% over 5m.
RuntimeBot: deploy-bot: "rolling: runtime+loader handshake v0.9 deployed to canary cluster - watch canary/quant-handshake dashboards" :rocket:
Jordan: I'll sketch the handshake proto & rpc today: negotiate(manifest_header) -> {support:true/false, reserved_kernels:[ids], reason}. Also runtime.rebind(model_id, new_profile) with timeout.
Maya: I'll capture telemetry schema and add SRE alert rules.
Priya: I'll draft QA matrix and a small test harness repo with simulated devices.
Sanjay: I'll append an RFC appendix documenting semantics for declarative-reserve vs force-rebind and permissioning (which customers can opt into aggressive requant).
Maya: timeline? canary by EOW?
Jordan: aiming for canary Mon-Tue, but need loader patch PR today.
Sanjay: cool — tagging @eng-runtime and @sre to review. Closing thread once PR is opened. 
Maya: thanks all. :thumbsup:
